answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and misbehavior slashes it. Reputation accrues slowly, like water whispering through karst - hidden channels carve trust over time, not overnight. A newcomer stands on flat mesa ground with no history, so counterparties demand escrow or tiny trial trades first. Cloning identities multiplies deposits, not trust, so faking a crowd costs more than it earns.
